about: Hand-written PROJECTS for the other AIs (owner rule 10, 2026-10-08: 'share workload with Grok; when it completes a task give it another; there should always be something for all other agents to work on'). Since 2026-10-09 most work is generated homework (tools/agents/homework.py from docs/agents/roles.json; docs/agents/RESEARCH_LOOP.md): this file keeps only what cannot be computed from the data (work in progress, code reviews, guides, music, motion, onboarding). A task with `reserves` holds those coins of those kinds for its AI while it is open. Each AI's page (docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md, the same text as its Drive doc 'WORK QUEUE for ...') shows: finish first (state now), then its homework, then the other projects.

agents.name: Grok
agents.strength: Strongest outside contributor (Numista sweep 9/10, story fixes 10/10; best blind photo test so far): web + Drive access, opens Numista, careful sources.
agents.reach: Drive doc 'WORK QUEUE for Grok' in Titan Reliquary/ + this repo (raw GitHub URLs)

tasks.title: UI rethink, part 1: a structure beyond the wings + a working prototype
tasks.what: Joseph wants the interface rethought from scratch, keeping every function: read the brief: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/titan-reliquary-preview/main/docs/design/REDESIGN_BRIEF.md (a copy is in Drive 'Titan Reliquary/design-incoming (AI UI proposals)/DESIGN BRIEF'), then open the live app on a phone-sized screen. Your part is the information architecture. (1) A proposal (.md): two structures that replace the five wings (for example one continuous space with semantic zoom from the whole collection down to one coin's die; or the coin as the centre that every view orbits), pick one and say why, and map every function in the brief's table to a place in it. (2) A working prototype (.html, Three.js from cdnjs with an exact version is fine) of its core move on the real data (../../../data/index.json and data/detail/{ISO}.json): open the app, see the whole collection, go to one coin and back, with the transition explaining where the coin lives. Phone first, 55+ fps, honours prefers-reduced-motion. Save both as design_grok_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}_{name}.md / .html in Drive 'design-incoming (AI UI proposals)'. Everything you need is in the brief; never invent coin data.
tasks.done_when: The proposal and the prototype are in the folder; Claude hosts the prototype at /prototypes/v2/grok/ and Joseph tries it on his phone.

tasks.title: Fact-check the coin stories, C151 to C283
tasks.what: Your first 18 fixes (C161 to C262, changes_grok-bot_20261008-1101/1102/1103) are merged: every one checked out. (While this is open, nobody else is given these stories: they are reserved for you.)
tasks.done_when: Every story from C151 to C283 checked; a list of the ones you changed and why (in your FEEDBACK doc note).

tasks.title: Album prices: a second source for the 10 most expensive holes
tasks.what: Your A001-A016 list is live as 'Cost to complete' (collection/prices/wants_values_grok_20261010-1949.json). The key dates look low against dealer guides (1921-D dime $140 at VF, where APMEX's lowest grade starts near $158). For the 10 most expensive holes in that file (A006 1916-D, 1921-D, 1921, 1923-S, 1926-S, 1927-D, 1916-S, 1918-D; A012 1949-D; A007 1964-D), find a second price page (PCGS CoinFacts, NGC Price Guide, Greysheet retail or APMEX) for the same grade, and send wants_values_grok_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json with the same shape; where the two sources differ by more than 25 %, give the higher and name both in source.
tasks.done_when: One file in reviews-incoming; Claude checks a sample and the app's total updates.

tasks.title: Music: a recording for each of the 3 held pieces
tasks.what: Held in docs/music/wanted.json: Elgar Nimrod, Debussy Rêverie (only a saxophone arrangement found so far), Satie Gymnopédie 3 on piano (the search keeps finding No. 1). Handel's Largo is done: Lea Desandre with Les Arts Florissants (CC BY 3.0) is live since 2026-10-09. For each held piece, find one Wikimedia Commons file that is a real performance of exactly that piece (not a synth or MIDI render), public domain or CC BY / CC BY-SA, with the performer named; give the exact Commons file title, the license and the performer, the same way as your 2026-10-08 music check. Save it as music_grok_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json in Drive 'music-requests'.
tasks.done_when: One JSON file with an exact Commons title (or 'none found' and why) for each held piece.

tasks.title: UI rethink, part 3: what is clunky today (phone walkthrough) + 10 references
tasks.what: Joseph wants the interface rethought from scratch, keeping every function: read the brief: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/titan-reliquary-preview/main/docs/design/REDESIGN_BRIEF.md (a copy is in Drive 'Titan Reliquary/design-incoming (AI UI proposals)/DESIGN BRIEF'). tasks.title: Cost to complete the albums: price the missing coins in A017 to A033
tasks.what: Joseph's dad asks which coins are missing; the next question is what they cost. Open https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/titan-reliquary-preview/main/data/wants.json: every album volume lists `missing_named` (the exact year and mint of each empty hole). For the volumes A017 to A033, find a retail price for each missing coin in a typical collectable grade (say which grade you assumed), from a named price page (PCGS CoinFacts, NGC Price Guide, Numista's value table, or a dealer's listed price for that exact date and mint). Never guess: leave a coin out when no page covers it. Silver coins are never below melt (spot in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/titan-reliquary-preview/main/data/prices.json). Save one file wants_values_muse_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json in Drive 'reviews-incoming (AI deep reviews)': a list of {"album": "A001", "label": "1941-D", "value_usd": 1.25, "grade": "VF", "source": "exact page URL", "confidence": "med|low"}, plus a total per album.
tasks.done_when: One JSON file covering every missing coin in A017 to A033 you could price; Claude checks a sample of the prices and adds a 'cost to complete' line to What's missing.

tasks.title: UI rethink, part 2: novel data views + a better atmosphere (two prototypes)
tasks.what: Joseph wants the interface rethought from scratch, keeping every function: read the brief: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/titan-reliquary-preview/main/docs/design/REDESIGN_BRIEF.md (a copy is in Drive 'Titan Reliquary/design-incoming (AI UI proposals)/DESIGN BRIEF'). Antigravity is the best surface for this (it can run and test code). Build two working prototypes on the real data, each one .html (or a small .zip), phone first: (A) a novel way to show the collection's data that a list or a card cannot (for example albums as a physical binder whose holes fill with the real phone photos and whose empty holes show what is missing and its price; the collection on a globe or timeline that morphs as you scroll; value as something that moves with the metal price). (B) a replacement for Scene Studio, which Joseph calls clunky: picking a World, its sound and the motion level in one smooth control with a live preview, instead of a long panel. Each with a short .md: the idea in one sentence, how it works on a phone, what it costs. Save as design_gemini_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}_{name}.{html|md|zip} in Drive 'design-incoming (AI UI proposals)'. Read data with ../../../data/... paths (Claude hosts it at /prototypes/v2/gemini/); never invent coin data; no edits to a copy of the app.
tasks.done_when: Both prototypes and their notes are in the folder; Claude hosts them at /prototypes/v2/gemini/.
